uncultured.finding: An archival protest-series photograph was inspected as structure rather than illustration: one uncovered frontal face is embedded in a field of repeated covered faces, while incense creates a strong vertical axis. The useful relation is visibility versus repeated concealment, not the literal identities of participants.
uncultured.candidate: A future remix can test whether repetition + one exposed exception + vertical ritual axis transfers to unrelated imagery without turning the source into decorative collage.
uncultured.production: No new artwork this round; source was deliberately held at structural-extraction stage to avoid premature remixing.
uncultured.next: pair this structure with an unrelated non-protest image and test whether the relation survives; continue JPG/PNG insertion separately

terminus.finding: A comparative labor-migration interview report shows that lowering one formal barrier does not settle participation or attachment: longer permitted stays reduce training costs and can stabilize trust, yet interviewees still describe exploitation, brokerage, cultural conflict, sector exit after residency, and divergent migrant preferences.
terminus.generated: THRESHOLD STACK: entry-format and action-scope thresholds are only the visible front gates. After entry, participation can still be constrained by dependency, intermediary power, rights, trust, exit options and whether actors actually want durable attachment. Lowering a threshold changes the feasible action set; it does not by itself create commitment.
terminus.next: seek a case where lowering entry barriers does produce durable participation, to distinguish threshold effects from downstream institutional conditions
